title: Direct Sample-Average Learning for Queueing Control: Gradient-Free Top-$K$ Coarse-to-Fine Optimization
summary: We study steady-state queueing control when decisions must be learned from a single persistent operating trajectory: only the implemented action produces data, and the queue is not reset when the action changes. Fixed-event-count cycles yield a direct ratio-of-totals sample-average approximation (SAA) of each action's steady-state cost rate. A Top-K coarse-to-fine search ranks these estimates, retains several promising refinement paths, and concentrates later operation on finer candidate sets, without requiring gradients, convexity, or differentiability.
